title: Joe Oliver as a fun-loving man; his wife and death
summary: Oliver was full of jokes, played opposite Dominique and Louis in Chicago cabarets; talk of his wife, daughter and where he died.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Well, there's a couple other fellas here on the list. Joe Oliver, can you tell us what kind of a fella he was?

Fine fella. Swell guy. Full of fun. I work right opposite. Louie and I work opposite. And don't think, cause Louie and I was across the street. Joe Oliver had Bob Schauffer. And he also had Kid Ory. He had Joyce Field there, too. He had Kid Ory with him. Don't think the plantation was packed. Like our place was packed. Both in cabaret right opposite each other. It was packed. Danny had the apex across the street after hours. All the places would be packed. It was a good day. Yeah, it was a good day. Bob Schauffer was with him. Bob Schauffer was with Joe. He stayed with Joe a long time.
Same Bob Schauffer. Now, Joe was full of fun. Full of fun.

Was it easy to get along with? Easy to get along with. My estimation. He used to come across there, joke with us. Always had some joke. He asked me one day, what size hat you wear? I said, I wear a seven. He said, no, you wear a twelve and a half. I said, alright, kid. Then he'd do this at Louie. He said, Louie, apart from you, you can smell the rice cooking in China. And hold his hand up to his nose? To his nose, yeah. Full of fun. He was life of the pie. What was he said to Louie? Smell the rice cooking in China.
Louie knew what he meant then. Yeah, he knew what he meant. And he hold his finger up.
And he had to laugh. He was so comical. Louie had to laugh himself. Louie knew what he meant. He wasn't sure.
Louie knew what he meant. Did you know Joe's wife or...
Yeah, I did. I did. Very nice person. I don't know why she moved.
She's still in New Orleans. I never met her. I don't know if she's in New Orleans.
She's in Chicago. Even her daughter. I don't know where they went. They said her daughter was in New York the last time.
But I don't know where they went to, where Mrs. Oliver. Joe died in Topeka, Kansas, I think.
